title: Vertical value hypotheses deck — sales quick test
content:
Slide 1 — Title: Vertical value hypotheses (sales quick test) — purpose: give AE/SEs a compact, testable set of value claims to surface with prospects across 4 target verticals. Not a final battlecard; playground to run a few discovery calls and validate.

Slide 2 — TL;DR (for quick skim):
- We believe Redwood's primary win conditions vary by vertical: cost/throughput for contact centers; data residency + compliance for healthcare; latency and integration simplicity for commerce personalization; model-guardrails and explainability for finserv.
- Key ask for sales: run these 5 targeted questions, measure prospect sensitivity to latency vs cost, and report back with a signed metric (cost % uptime, latency p95 target, or compliance blocker).

Slide 3 — How to use this deck (AE quick play):
- Open with the prospect's top KPI (revenue per session, handle time, compliance risk).
- Run the vertical-specific discovery script below.
- Offer 1 quick experiment: 2-week POC on hosted API (if low regulatory needs) or dedicated 1-week pilot (if throughput or residency matter).
- Capture one success metric and the expected rollout window (Q vs 6–12 months).

Slide 4 — Questions to prioritize on every call (short):
- What is your primary cost sensitivity? (per-request vs sustained throughput)
- What latency SLO is unforgivable? (e.g., p95 < 300ms, < 800ms, etc.)
- Do you require tenant isolation / VPC / on-prem?
- How often do models change or do you require model versioning/audits?
- What data classification (PII/PHI) & retention rules apply?

Slide 5 — Vertical: Contact centers (hypotheses + messaging)
Hypotheses:
- Primary driver: reduce average handle time (AHT) and deflection using real-time LLM features; customers prioritize p95 latency and steady throughput more than raw model fidelity.
- Secondary driver: per-agent token cost; predictable monthly billing is crucial.

Sales messaging:
- Lead with latency & fallback story: "We can guarantee sub-300ms p95 in Dedicated for passage-length prompts; fallback to a smaller variant warms within seconds."
- Cost hook: show batching & prefix-caching can cut token usage by ~20–40% on typical transcripts.

POC ask: 3-week pilot with 10 agents, compare AHT & CSAT baseline vs Redwood-enhanced routing.

Slide 6 — Vertical: Healthcare (hypotheses + messaging)
Hypotheses:
- Primary driver: data residency, audit trails, and key mgmt. Customers often need Private deployment or VPC with HSM integration.
- Secondary driver: model explainability and safe-fail behaviors; clinicians need visible provenance of suggestions.

Sales messaging:
- Compliance-first angle: "Private mode + KMS integration + audit logs — we can run ingestion in your VPC and keep logs for X days; we also support HL7 payloads via our ingestion templates."
- Explainability talk track: offer structured outputs and token-level provenance for top-3 suggestions.

POC ask: sandbox deployment within their VPC for a week with 2 clinicians and audit log export.

Slide 7 — Vertical: Commerce / Personalization (hypotheses + messaging)
Hypotheses:
- Primary driver: latency at scale (page load or microservice tail) and cost per inference at high qps; integration simplicity wins over marginal model quality improvements.
- Secondary driver: model caching & KV reuse across sessions reduces cost materially.

Sales messaging:
- Performance angle: "We optimize kernels and routing to keep p50/p95 within your storefront thresholds, and provide pre-built adapters for common personalization platforms."
- Economics: show short model matrix (7B quantized vs 70B float) with cost/latency tradeoffs for expected qps.

POC ask: A/B on a single personalization point for three traffic slices for two weeks.

Slide 8 — Vertical: Financial services (hypotheses + messaging)
Hypotheses:
- Primary driver: traceability, reproducible rollouts, and guardrails to avoid hallucinations.
- Secondary driver: auditability and model-version pinning for regulatory reporting.

Sales messaging:
- Governance angle: "Pin a model version across rollout, enforce eval suites, and we can provide audit exports aligned with your compliance team."
- Risk mitigation: run canary rollouts + automatic fallback to deterministic templates when confidence thresholds are low.

POC ask: 30-day guarded pilot on a low-risk workflow (e.g., summarization of public filings) with model pinning and evals enabled.

Slide 9 — Common objections + rebuttals (quick bullets)
- Objection: "We can self-host cheaper." Rebuttal: "We’ve benchmarked end-to-end cost including infra ops; Dedicated plus Optimize gives predictable unit economics and offloads the operational burden that typically doubles E2E cost."
- Objection: "Latency is too variable." Rebuttal: "We provide latency SLOs and routing policies; canary to dedicated with fallback to smaller variants for tail reduction."
- Objection: "We need on-prem only." Rebuttal: "Private on-prem options exist; we can scope a minimum viable private pilot and offer data plane only installs if needed."

Slide 10 — Quick technical cheatsheet for SEs (talking points)
- Hosted API: fastest time-to-value, pay-as-you-go, limited residency. Good for early experiments and non-PII.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput, SLA-backed latency. Good for mid-scale workloads and high QPS.
- Private: VPC/on-prem, KMS/HSM integrations, full audit. Good for regulated & sensitive data.
- Optimize levers: batching, prefix/KV caching, quantization profiles, model routing. Give customers 2 knobs to play with (e.g., reduce latency window or reduce cost by X%).

Slide 11 — Example pricing narratives (short)
- Commerce: show per-inference tiered price with committed throughput discount.
- Contact center: avg cost per conversation + surge capacity pricing.
- Healthcare/FinServ: platform fee + support + optional compliance retainer.

Slide 12 — Experimental playbook (how we validate these hypotheses)
- Run 12 targeted discovery calls (3 per vertical) in next 4 weeks.
- For each call capture: key KPI, target latency SLO, cost sensitivity bucket, and whether VPC/private required.
- Run 4 pilots (one per vertical) with clear success metrics.
- Collate results into a one-pager and update this deck with real numbers and customer quotes.

Slide 13 — Data to collect from AE after call (short form)
- Prospect name, ARR band, top KPI to improve, must-have compliance requirements, desired p95 latency, expected monthly qps, pilot willingness, decision timeline.

Slide 14 — Open questions for product/eng (items we need to get before next iteration)
- Need recent throughput & p95 numbers for 7B quantized vs 13B and 70B float on Dedicated (NVIDIA H100 baseline) and Hosted. (Action: Marco to pull benchmark matrix)
- Confirm private deployment minimum scope (disk, networking, SLA) and expected delivery lead time. (Action: SRE/Private team)
- Template for HL7 ingestion & audit log export for healthcare pilot. (Action: Solutions eng)

Slide 15 — Next steps & owners
- Aisha: run outreach to top 12 targets and collect discovery forms (due in 3 weeks).
- Evelyn: draft pilot contracts & data processing addendum for healthcare and finserv pilots.
- Marco: compile the latency/cost matrix and add to slide appendix.
- Liam: create a light demo script & sandbox creds for pilots.

Appendix — rough numbers we want to show once compiled:
- p95 latencies: hosted small model ~120–250ms; hosted large ~500–900ms; dedicated small ~80–200ms; dedicated large ~300–600ms. (PLACEHOLDER — engineering to confirm)
- Typical token savings from prefix caching on conversational flows: 15–35%.
- Expected throughput per GPU by model family: placeholder numbers; will fill after benchmark run.

Notes to self: keep slide deck lean for AEs (8–12 slides for call prep); move deep tech and benchmark table to appendix. Collect customer quotes and update messaging for each vertical after pilot results.

Unresolved: whether to include explicit per-token numbers in a public-facing slide vs share only in private proposal.
